Use-case & requirements summary (customer-supplied):
- Workloads: conversational support for traders (low-latency chat), live reranking of candidate responses, high-quality embeddings for near-real-time search.
- Latency targets: p50 <30ms, p95 <120ms end-to-end from user keystroke to tokens rendered.
- Throughput: baseline 150 QPS, burst 600 QPS (10s bursts).
- Cost sensitivity: unit economics tight; prefer quantized model variants + intelligent batching; exploring dynamic batching vs static per-tenant pools.
- Model preferences: open Llama-family style model tuned for finance; will accept INT8/4 quantized variants if quality delta <2% on eval set.
- Routing/fallback: primary low-latency model, fallback to larger higher-latency model for complex prompts; seamless model pinning per-customer.
- Observability: need token-level cost attribution, per-route latency histograms, and per-request trace linking to business transaction ids.
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress, must support SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, audit logs for 1 year; EU customers require data residency option.

POC / acceptance criteria (from SE call):
- Run Redwood dedicated config with suggested batching/caching settings on a 3-day perf run against their production-like replay.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tail behavior when KV cache hit-rate drops, and cost per 1k tokens.
- Quantization step: run same workload on FP16 vs INT8 + kernel choices to quantify accuracy delta and cost savings.
- Must show <120ms p95 and <=20% increase in error/quality metric vs FP16 baseline.

Notes from customer quotes / color: "We can tolerate occasional higher latency for long contextual completions but not for the trader UI — that has to feel instant." — Head of Product.
